counting_convention: A key counts as a countable complete H2 only when the source supplies the concrete non-routine author core for the full target as stated, every part covered, leaving only mechanical completion or restatement. H2_material_incomplete_full_target, H1_as_support_only, H1_residual_recommendation, external_author_core_pending and grouped rows are not countable. This is the same standard the independent reviewer applied.

rulings.deciding_printed_evidence: Comment physical 638 (printed 621), lines 44-47: 'Let mu_omega2 and nu_omega2 be the conditional distributions of omega1 and omega3 given omega2. Then let (omega1, omega2, omega3) have the law where (omega1, omega3) has conditional law mu_omega2 x nu_omega2 given omega2. See Exercise 18.20 of Billingsley (1995) for a general construction from specified conditional distributions. One can also make a similar construction for finite A and then use Kolmogorov's existence theorem.' The exercise asks for a coupling with ordered marginals, and the recombination printed here is the whole mechanism that produces it; the ordered support follows from the witnesses the two kernels are read off.
rulings.why_the_owner_label_stands: It does survive. Owner, independent and both comparison columns of the independent report keep this row in the H2 family; the owner's own H2_core_complete flag is true.
rulings.why_the_model_tier_does_not_supersede: The model's action string external_author_core_pending is about where the existence theorem lives, not about whether the author supplies the mechanism: its own concrete_remaining_burden describes the same recombination and calls the remainder technical. A cited general measurability tool named by the author is not the non-routine idea of the exercise, and the counting convention counts the author core, not the availability of every cited theorem in the bounded input. The tier 'H1' in the same row is a difficulty proposal, and the input instructed the model to keep material state and difficulty separate; a difficulty tier cannot change a material family.
residues_kept_literal: The exercise writes P1 dominated by P2 and P2 dominated by P3; the flattened glyphs in the text layer are not repaired here. Both literals retained.

The existence of regular conditional distributions is cited out to Billingsley (1995), Exercise 18.20, and to Kolmogorov's existence theorem for the finite-A route. The judging opinion above records this as a named external tool the author disposes of in one sentence, not as an unprinted core; the owner's own confidence on this row is medium, and the alternative reading is kept open below.

rulings.deciding_printed_evidence: Comment physical 638 (printed 621), lines 49-52 cover part (a) only: 'Given eps > 0, let R be large enough that the balls of radius R satisfy P[B_R(x) intersects omega] > 1 - eps for every vertex x', then 'every infinite component K of G minus F contains a ball of radius R and therefore intersects omega with probability more than 1 - eps', closing 'Since this holds for all finite F, the result follows.' Part (b), p_u(G) = 1 for quasi-transitive G with more than one end, has no printed text anywhere in the Chapter 7 comments block.
rulings.why_the_owner_label_stands: It does survive. Owner and independent agree on the literal family label, both record H2_core_complete false, and the owner's counted_H2_note already forbids reading this row as a third countable core.
rulings.why_the_model_tier_does_not_supersede: The model itself concedes both material facts: that the hint does not deliver the passage to an end-convergent subset inside a prescribed end, and that 'part (b) has no supplied proof material at all'. Its H1 is therefore not a finding that the target is fully printed; it is the same material state labelled by difficulty. Filing a half-unprinted target as low difficulty would make the difficulty column contradict the material column, so the family label stands.

The owner's concrete_core compresses part (b) to 'with more than one end, pu = 1'. That sentence is the target of (b), not a proof of it; it is not counted as material here.

rulings.deciding_printed_evidence: Comment physical 638-639 (printed 621-622). Solution 1: 'This follows from (6.13) and the proof of Proposition 6.6.' Solution 2 prints the supermultiplicativity display 'P_o[X_n = o] >= P_o[X_k = o] P_o[X_{n-k} = o]', then 'Thus, by Fekete's lemma (Exercise 3.9), we have rho(G) = lim_n P_o[X_n = o]^{1/n} as well as P_o[X_n = o] <= rho(G)^n for all n', and then the parity sentence 'if P_o[X_k = o] = 0 for odd k, it is still true that P_o[X_k = o] is strictly positive for all even k, whence lim_n P_o[X_{2n} = o]^{1/2n} exists and equals rho(G)'. Both requested statements - the even-time limit and the pointwise bound - are covered by printed steps, and no input outside the same book is used.
rulings.why_the_owner_label_stands: It does survive. Owner and independent agree on H2 with H2_core_complete true; this row has the least material dispute of the scope.
